title: Zhoukoudian: Peking Man (Homo erectus)
summary: At Zhoukoudian, 42 km southwest of Beijing, excavations found the remains of "Peking Man", Homo erectus, with stone tools. Burial dating of quartz in the lower cultural layers of Locality 1 gave about 0.77 million years, roughly 200,000 years older than earlier estimates, which suggests these early humans lived through cold glacial conditions.

uncertainty.note: Weighted mean 0.77 ± 0.08 Myr for lower cultural layers 7–10; Purdue gives the site as 680,000–780,000 years old.

as_recorded.value: Homo erectus pekinensis , who lived in the Middle Pleistocene (700,000 to 200,000 years ago)

where.modern_name: Peking Man Site at Zhoukoudian, Fangshan District, Beijing, China
where.historical_name: Zhoukoudian cave deposits, Middle Pleistocene northern China (no polity)

importance.justification: One of the first Homo erectus sites found, whose reassessed age changed views of early humans in cold northern China.

sources.title: Age of Zhoukoudian Homo erectus determined with 26Al/10Be burial dating
sources.author: Shen, Gao, Gao & Granger

sources.title: New dating method finds Peking Man older than thought

reviewer_note: Least sure that 0.77 Ma covers all Peking Man remains: it dates the lower layers 7–10 only, and UNESCO gives the broader 700,000–200,000 year range.
